newsitem.title: UK: BA says any strikes to depress profits.
newsitem.headline: BA says any strikes to depress profits.

text.p: British Airways Plc, which is facing potential strike action by trade unions, warned on Thursday that the task of bringing back customers after any disruption would help depress current year profits.

The costs associated with what it called "exceptional contingency measures" to handle potential industrial action would also hit earnings, BA said, adding that the continued strength of sterling would also exacerbate pressure on reported yields.

BA, which said the threat of strike action was already having an impact of forward bookings, earlier sent a proposal to arbitration service ACAS to try and settle a dispute with cabin crew as a strike deadline loomed.

The airline's stewards and stewardesses have threatened a three-day strike next week over plans to restructure pay and conditions, which are part of BA's plans to save 1.0 billion pounds ($1.7 billion) by the end of the century.
Officials from the Transport & General Workers trade unions say the package would cut cabin crew salaries and have bristled at BA sealing a deal with the smaller Cabin Crew 89 union.

A BA spokesman has said the airline's proposal addressed two main concerns -- the union's fears about its members being worse off under the new arrangement, and the relationships between the two cabin crew unions.

BA also faces trouble on the ground, where staff voted last week for strike action to protest the sale of the catering unit at London's Heathrow airport, part of BA's drive to outsource more non-core services.
By 1555 GMT, BA's shares slid 8.5p to 682.5p.
